name: transit_plan
description: Plan a public transit journey between two endpoints. Each endpoint is either a stop id (from_stop_id / to_stop_id, sent to the planner verbatim) or a coordinate pair (from_lat+from_lon / to_lat+to_lon); the two endpoints may use different forms, but supplying both forms for one endpoint is invalid_input/mixed_endpoint_form. `time` may be an explicit offset-bearing instant (passed through unchanged, never re-read or shifted), a naive local clock, a date-only value (its local midnight), or omitted (now). A naive clock or date is read in the endpoint zone that owns the decision: the origin for a depart_after search, and the destination zone for an arrive_by search, so 'be there by 18:00' means the destination's 18:00. A deliberate `timezone` supplies that reading explicitly; origin_timezone / destination_timezone declare an endpoint's display zone, which the response echoes per endpoint. A naive clock skipped by a DST gap is rejected as invalid_input/nonexistent_local_time naming the gap, and a repeated clock as invalid_input/ambiguous_local_time with both candidate offsets and instants - never resolved silently; the remedy is an explicit offset instant or a zone. The result is one canonical envelope: time_frame, query (the effective query echo: control, requested and effective instant, search_window_seconds, minimum_requested, upstream_count, returned_count, max_results, truncated/truncation_reason/dropped_count, both page cursors, requested/applied modes, realtime_present), from/to place objects, itineraries in upstream order, direct street-only alternatives when include_direct is true, constraints_active, and warnings. Itineraries and legs carry one canonical timestamp object per instant, each rendered in its own endpoint's zone (zone is null with zone_source unavailable when the payload supplied none). This is a bounded search context, not a whole-day optimum: nothing is re-sorted, de-duplicated or selected as best, and max_results truncates after upstream ordering with truncated and truncation_reason reporting the cut. continuation holds previous and next, each a cursor frozen together with the complete effective query; replay by passing that object alone, and any contradicting argument is rejected as invalid_input/cursor_without_identical_query naming every differing field. An empty answer is outcome no_routes with no_routes_reason (street_only_alternatives_returned or not_determined) plus constraints_active; it never claims which supplied constraint caused it. Durations are integer seconds and an unknown value is null, never zero. RAIL is a parent mode covering high-speed, long-distance, night, regional, suburban and subway classes, so it is not 'mainline only'; REGIONAL_RAIL, LONG_DISTANCE, METRO and SUBWAY are the values that distinguish service classes. Street modes are rejected as street_mode_not_transit and unknown spellings as unknown_mode.

from_stop_id.description: Origin stop id, sent verbatim (exactly one form per endpoint)

to_stop_id.description: Destination stop id, sent verbatim (exactly one form per endpoint)

time.description: Explicit offset instant (2026-10-27T09:00:00Z), naive local clock (2026-10-27T09:00) read at the rotated endpoint, or date (2026-10-27) for its local midnight; omitted means now. Never an offset-less value sent upstream.

arrive_by.description: false = depart after `time` (origin local); true = arrive by it (destination local)

timezone.description: Caller IANA zone used to read a naive clock; a deliberate frame, never an endpoint claim

origin_timezone.description: Declared origin display zone (IANA); outranks stop/discovery evidence

destination_timezone.description: Declared destination display zone (IANA); outranks stop/discovery evidence

transit_modes.description: Accepted transit modes, sent in caller order as one comma-joined value. RAIL is a parent mode covering high-speed, long-distance, night, regional, suburban and subway classes, not mainline only.

num_itineraries.description: Minimum itineraries requested; echoed as query.minimum_requested

max_itineraries.description: Upstream computation cap; approximate, never a returned-result limit

max_results.description: Strict wrapper cap applied after upstream ordering; the only thing that makes truncated meaningful. Omit to return every supplied itinerary.

query.description: The frozen effective query returned beside that cursor; it is the authority and is validated with the same rules as a first call

continuation.description: Pass continuation.previous or continuation.next from a previous result, alone. A separately supplied argument that contradicts the frozen query is rejected as cursor_without_identical_query naming the fields.

include_direct.description: Include the upstream's street-only direct alternatives when non-empty

max_access_walk_minutes.description: Access walk cap per endpoint, in minutes (sent as maxPreTransitTime)

max_egress_walk_minutes.description: Egress walk cap per endpoint, in minutes (sent as maxPostTransitTime)

min_transfer_minutes.description: Minimum transfer time, in minutes (sent as minTransferTime)

name: transit_geocode
description: Resolve a place name, address or stop to canonical matches. `types` restricts the match kinds (ADDRESS, PLACE, STOP) and `modes` filters stops by available transport modes; both are sent upstream as one comma-joined value in the caller's order rather than enforced client-side. RAIL in `modes` does not separate mainline from Metro: it expands to the rail-ish classes including subway. `near` (a lat/lon pair) biases the ranking toward that coordinate and filters nothing; `near_bias` (0..1) sets how strongly. A single-result request is not a disambiguation strategy, and dataset names differ from colloquial names, so refine the query text instead of assuming the first hit is meant. Every match reports name, match_type, match_id, stop_id, lat, lon, modes, importance, country, timezone, score, category, street, house_number, zip, level and areas. stop_id is populated only when match_type is STOP, and is then the same value as match_id because that identifier is accepted by the planner; for ADDRESS and PLACE matches stop_id is null and match_id is the only identifier. The geocode Match schema carries no parent grouping, so no parent_id is returned and no enrichment request is made; use transit_nearby_stops for parent grouping. num_results defaults to 10 and is bounded 1..40 and is a request parameter, not a client-side slice; count is the number of matches the upstream returned.

query.description: Place name, address or stop name

types.description: Restrict match kinds; sent as one comma-joined `type` value

modes.description: Filter stops by available transport modes; sent as one `mode` value

name: transit_departures
description: Live departure board for one stop id (from transit_geocode or transit_nearby_stops). `time` follows the transit_plan forms: an explicit offset-bearing instant is sent unchanged, while a naive clock or date-only value is read in the stop's own zone, resolved from stop metadata with at most one lookup and overridable by `timezone` or the deliberate `endpoint_timezone`; a skipped or repeated local clock is rejected rather than guessed. count defaults to 10 (1..50) and `window` is an optional 1..86400 second span. Each departure keeps scheduled and realtime apart: scheduled_departure is the timetable time, expected_departure is populated only when the payload carries realtime and a departure value, realtime comes from the required StopTime.realTime flag (a body omitting it is malformed_upstream), and `scheduled` is always null because the pinned StopTime has no such property - realtime availability says nothing about whether the service was originally scheduled and is never its negation. delay_seconds is expected minus scheduled in integer seconds, or null when either is absent. trip_cancelled and stop_cancelled are tri-state: true, false, or null when the payload is silent.

time.description: Explicit offset instant, naive clock or date; omitted means now

timezone.description: Caller IANA zone for a naive clock

name: transit_nearby_stops
description: Find the nearest transit stops around a coordinate. radius is in metres, 1..5000, default 1000, and becomes the request's bounding box. Results are the nearest 20 stops inside that radius, nearest first, each with stop_id, name, lat, lon, distance_m and the stop metadata the map payload supplies (modes, timezone, parent_id, vertex_type); an absent member is null and never fabricated, and no enrichment request is made. Coverage is the requested window's results, not a guaranteed global nearest set: near a pole, or at a clamped antimeridian edge, a stop inside the radius can fall outside the box the upstream was asked for, and a stop the upstream never returns cannot be reported. count is the post-truncation length and truncated is the cut signal.

name: transit_reverse_geocode
description: Convert coordinates to the closest places, stops or addresses. `types` restricts the match kinds (ADDRESS, PLACE, STOP) and `num_results` (1..40) bounds how many are requested; both are omitted from the request unless supplied, leaving the upstream's own defaults in force. Each match reports name, match_type, match_id, stop_id, lat, lon and the metadata the payload supplies. stop_id is populated only for a STOP match and then equals match_id; ADDRESS and PLACE matches carry stop_id null. The Match schema carries no parent grouping, so no parent_id is returned and no enrichment request is made.

name: transit_trip
description: Full stop sequence for one trip id from transit_plan or transit_departures. The tool takes no time input, so every time is rendered from the payload's own endpoint zones rather than re-read in a caller frame. Each leg reports index, mode, from/to places, departure/arrival, the scheduled pair when supplied, realtime and scheduled tri-states, the cancellation split (a failed street leg reports walking_route_unavailable and duration_is_estimate with cancelled null, while a transit leg reports its own cancelled), route, headsign, agency_name, intermediate_stop_count and intermediate_stops. Each intermediate stop reports stop_id, name, arrival, departure, the scheduled pair, track, cancelled and stop_cancelled; a place that is an endpoint of a failed street path is never reported as a cancelled stop.

trip_id.description: Trip id from transit_plan or transit_departures

name: transit_health
description: Check whether the Transitous API server is healthy. Returns a raw provider payload: the upstream response unchanged, not the canonical envelope, so its shape is the upstream's.

name: transit_reachable
description: Find places reachable from one coordinate within a travel-time budget. max_time_min is 1..1440 (default 60). The single `one` endpoint is the origin when arrive_by is false and the destination when arrive_by is true; query.one_role names which, and a naive clock is read in that endpoint's zone (overridable by `timezone` or `endpoint_timezone`) rather than in either of the places that merely happen to be reachable. Each entry reports name, lat, lon, travel_time_seconds (integer seconds from the payload's duration) and transfers_k verbatim (k=1 direct, k=2 one transfer): one seconds field, one name, no minute alias and no second change-counting definition. Both members are optional upstream, so an absent one is null, never zero. The result is the upstream's bounded reachable set, not a complete reachable area and not a time-band guarantee.

time.description: Explicit offset instant, naive clock or date; omitted means now

arrive_by.description: false = `one` is the origin; true = `one` is the destination

timezone.description: Caller IANA zone for a naive clock

name: transit_refresh
description: Re-fetch one itinerary with real-time updates, using itinerary_id from transit_plan. Returns a raw provider payload: the upstream response unchanged, not the canonical envelope. Failures still use the canonical error result.

name: transit_rentals
description: Find nearby shared bikes, scooters and cars (GBFS sharing systems). Returns a raw provider payload: the upstream response unchanged, not the canonical envelope. Failures still use the canonical error result.

name: transit_one_to_many
description: Street durations from one coordinate to 1..50 destinations. No clock is involved, so no time is accepted or reported. `one` (from_lat/from_lon) is the origin, or the destination when arrive_by is true; query.one_role states which and the destination array supplies the other side. The server may impose its own maximum street duration; no wrapper guarantee overrides that limit. Results are indexed to the requested destination order and carry the requested lat/lon plus duration_seconds and distance_meters from that index's Duration, preserving finite fractional values without rounding. An empty Duration is null/null, never zero. A missing or extra entry is malformed_upstream/unexpected_shape, and the result is no_routes only when every destination lacks a duration.

destinations.description: Destination [lat, lon] pairs, in result order

mode.description: Street profile; exactly WALK, BIKE or CAR

max_sec.description: Maximum street duration in seconds; finite and non-negative

arrive_by.description: false = many-to-one is off (`one` is origin); true = `one` is the destination

name: transit_one_to_many_transit
description: Street duration plus the transit Pareto set for every destination (1..50). `time` follows the transit_plan forms and a naive clock is read at the `one` endpoint's zone (overridable by `timezone` or `endpoint_timezone`); `one` is the origin for arrive_by false and the destination for arrive_by true, which query.one_role reports. Walking-minute names align with transit_plan; transit_modes defaults to ["TRANSIT"] and RAIL is a parent mode. query.applied_modes lists the modes actually applied in caller order, and those same values are sent upstream as one comma-joined transitModes value. Results are indexed to the requested destination order: street_duration_seconds, street_distance_meters and `transit`, an array of {duration_seconds, transfers} in supplied Pareto order. Pareto durations are the seconds as returned, and the upstream currently reports them at whole minutes' resolution, so they are not second-accurate. An empty Pareto set means no transit connection for that destination: it is an empty `transit` array with the street fields still populated, never a zero duration. Missing required Pareto members are malformed, not defaults, and transfers keeps the schema's own name.

destinations.description: Destination [lat, lon] pairs, in result order

time.description: Explicit offset instant, naive clock or date; omitted means now

arrive_by.description: false = one-to-many (`one` is origin); true = many-to-one (`one` is destination)

timezone.description: Caller IANA zone for a naive clock

name: transit_map_trips
description: Active trips inside a bounding box and time window. min_lat/min_lon/max_lat/max_lon are required, with corners in range and min strictly less than max on both axes; start_time is strictly before end_time; zoom is 1..19 (default 12), high zoom meaning local and low meaning long-distance. A bounding box has no single endpoint zone, so a naive (offset-less) start_time or end_time is invalid_input/bbox_window_requires_explicit_zone unless a caller `timezone` is supplied; explicit offset instants need no zone. Each trip segment reports trip_id, route, mode, from/to places, departure/arrival, the scheduled pair, from_lat/from_lon/to_lat/to_lon, distance_meters, polyline_present and realtime from the required TripSegment.realTime (a body omitting it is malformed_upstream). There is no vehicle_position field: the pinned schema has no position slot and no supported source provides one. At most 50 segments are returned; upstream_count, returned_count and truncated report the cut.

start_time.description: Explicit offset instant, or a naive clock with a caller timezone

end_time.description: Explicit offset instant, or a naive clock with a caller timezone

timezone.description: Caller IANA zone; the only way to read a naive window, because a bounding box has no endpoint zone
